title: Saltrent Systems — onboarding kickoff & runbook intake
summary: Kickoff for Saltrent's Redwood onboarding. Reviewed high-level goals (low-latency inference for customer support chatbot, data residency, and auditability), mapped stakeholders, discussed VPC/on-prem options and network requirements, and agreed on next steps: send pilot SOW, security pack, and runbook template. Identified a short pilot (2-4 weeks) to validate latency and RBAC flows.
topics: Intro & goals: latency, cost, data residency
Deployment form factor: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
Security controls: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS, SOC2
Network: egress rules, firewall IPs, peering, proxy
Runbook & ownership: sprint plan, staging, go-live checklist
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-28 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~73 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Rina Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jamie Lowe (CTO - Saltrent), Maya Reyes (DevOps), Carlos Mendes (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Security)
Shared artifacts: Saltrent kickoff deck (link: /files/saltrent-kickoff-deck.pdf), proposed pilot SOW (note: will be sent), security binder (link: https://redwood.app/security/saltrent)

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Avery, AE for Redwood Inference, and with me are Samir and Rina. quick check, am I on time?
[00:08] Jamie Lowe: yes we're good, thanks. zoomed in from SF office, excited to get the runbook started.
[00:14] Samir Patel: awesome, high level for today is align on goals, map stakeholders and network needs, and capture the runbook intake items so our onboarding team can spin up the pilot.
[00:23] Maya Reyes: sounds good. our primary use case is support chat automation, high concurrency during biz hours, and strict log retention — we need tokens and logs retained for 7 years for some compliance reasons, long story.
[00:35] Rina Kapoor: okay, thanks Maya. quick clarifying Q: is data residency a hard requirement for the pilot or for production later?
[00:41] Jamie Lowe: production. pilot can be hosted but we need to validate VPC and on-prem for later. we already have a legal review flagged for october.
[00:52] Avery Chen: good, that's consistent with other customers — recommended path is start with Redwood Hosted to accelerate time-to-value and run latency bench, then follow with a Dedicated or Private (VPC) ingest for production. we can schedule a private onboarding window.
[01:05] Carlos Mendes: when you say "Hosted" will logs ever leave our control? we need to see retention and ability to export.
[01:12] Samir Patel: yes, Hosted keeps logs in our control plane but you can configure retention, export S3 sinks, and we provide audit logs. we'll send the security pack that lists retention options and export mechanics.
[01:23] Priya Nair: also need to confirm KMS integration — we require customer-managed keys for payload encryption at rest.
[01:30] Rina Kapoor: we do KMS integration — we support AWS KMS and HSM integrations for Private. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption; customer-managed KMS for private deployments. small aside, sometimes S3 ACLs are misread in the docs, we'll include an example.
[01:45] Jamie Lowe: perfect. on networking, our infra sits in a locked VPC with strict egress rules. we'll likely want VPC peering or private link to avoid public egress.
[01:56] Avery Chen: understood. we have both VPC Peering and AWS PrivateLink options for Redwood Private; for Dedicated we can also set up session NAT with allowlists. We'll capture IP ranges and proxy requirements in the runbook.
[02:08] Maya Reyes: do you publish a static list of IPs? our security team hates ephemeral ranges.
[02:13] Rina Kapoor: yes — for Dedicated/Private we give stable egress endpoints and BGP routes if needed. Hosted's IPs are published but are more dynamic; if you need fully static endpoints, Private is the route.
[02:23] Carlos Mendes: great. what's the typical pilot footprint? GPU count, memory?
[02:29] Avery Chen: for a support bot pilot we usually provision a small Dedicated pool — 1-2 GPUs with 40-60 concurrent sessions in the window, depending on prompt length. if you want to exercise long context and evals we can provision a single A100-equivalent instance.
[02:41] Jamie Lowe: budget conversation — can you ballpark pilot cost?
[02:44] Samir Patel: we'll send a tailored SOW, but a two-week pilot with a small Dedicated footprint historically lands in the low thousands (USD), plus engineering time. I'll follow up with the estimate.
[02:56] Priya Nair: on compliance, we're SOC2 and ISO27001 scoped — we need logs, RBAC, SSO with SAML, and per-request audit logging. can you support fine-grain RBAC?
[03:08] Rina Kapoor: yes, Redwood Console supports org-level RBAC, route-level policies, and token scoping. note: tokens and tracing can be mapped to user ids for audit. sometimes the console name is transcribed as "Redwood Consolee" — ignore that, it's the same.
[03:24] Maya Reyes: and SSO?
[03:25] Samir Patel: SAML and OIDC supported; we'll help configure with your IdP. we also offer SCIM for provisioning.
[03:33] Jamie Lowe: good. on the ops side we need a runbook with a pre-prod checklist: env vars, KV cache warm, redis? we use internal redis and sidecar for feature flags. any special ops for KV cache?
[03:46] Rina Kapoor: KV cache is automatic inside the runtime, but if you use persistent cache layers we have guidance for warm-up and priming. we'll add a step-by-step for cache priming and a sample prod-rollout canary.
[03:58] Carlos Mendes: do you have a recommended canary percentage and rollbacks?
[04:01] Avery Chen: typical pattern is 5% canary for 24 hours, then 25% for 6-12 hours, and then full. we have built-in fallback policies to route to a cheaper model if latency spikes.
[04:12] Jamie Lowe: talk to me about metrics — token cost breakdowns and latency SLOs?
[04:18] Samir Patel: Console surfaces token-level cost and per-route latency histograms. for SLOs we can configure alerts and SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated customers. we'll show sample dashboards in the second session.
[04:31] Maya Reyes: who owns the instrumentation? we have a DataDog stack — can Redwood push traces?
[04:36] Rina Kapoor: yes, we have tracers and exporters for DataDog and Prometheus; we also provide webhooks for events and push logs to your S3.
[04:45] Jamie Lowe: ok. next up security deep-dive scheduling — can we do that with Priya next week?
[04:51] Priya Nair: yes, I'm free tuesday afternoon.
[04:54] Avery Chen: we'll pencil that in. (note: quick logistic) Samir will send a calendar invite for the security review with an initial questionnaire.
[05:02] Jamie Lowe: thanks. let's walk the onboarding runbook items now — Maya can drive any network specifics.
[05:09] Maya Reyes: Sure. step one: provide team contact matrix and management VLANs. step two: allowlist egress IPs and private link endpoints. step three: provide service account for SSO mapping and SCIM group. step four: test a simple inference call from staging.
[05:22] Rina Kapoor: I'll add those to the runbook. Any preference on staging naming conventions?
[05:26] Carlos Mendes: we use "stg-1" then promote to "stg-2" then prod; would like token scopes to match environment names.
[05:33] Samir Patel: that's common, can enforce that with route-level tokens.
[05:37] [00:06:00] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[05:40] Jamie Lowe: can you show a sample curl to hit the hosted API so our engineers can sanity check?
[05:44] Rina Kapoor: sure, sample I'll paste later in the notes: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' — note: some of the endpoint names differ, we'll provide the exact SDK snippets.
[05:59] Maya Reyes: perfect — SDKs are preferable (go, python, node) we use Go and Python primarily.
[06:06] Avery Chen: we support official SDKs and internal client libs. Rina will share the quickstart repo link.
[06:12] Rina Kapoor: link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart (note: sample repo name may change).
[06:20] Carlos Mendes: anything else for the pilot success criteria? we want a max p95 latency under 350ms and tail p99 under 700ms for short prompts.
[06:30] Rina Kapoor: achievable with Dedicated and right batching. we'll instrument and run load tests. we'll also recommend quantization settings if you want to reduce token cost.
[06:41] Priya Nair: can you do a legal/data residency memo that we can attach to the vendor review?
[06:46] Samir Patel: yes, Samir will send the security binder and a short data residency memo.
[06:50] Jamie Lowe: schedule-wise, we'd like to start pilot second week of October. is that feasible?
[06:58] Avery Chen: yes, we can aim to have the pilot window 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-26. we'll need sign-off on SOW and network allowlist by Oct 8 to make that cadence.
[07:10] Maya Reyes: next, runbook ownership — who is the main CSM for the onboarding?
[07:15] Samir Patel: Samir will own CSM tasks, Rina will be SE lead and Avery will be overall sponsor from sales. we'll capture ownership in the runbook.
[07:23] Jamie Lowe: good. any 3rd party integrations we should call out? We plan to use internal vector DB (we call it "VDB") plus Redis and Postgres.
[07:32] Rina Kapoor: note on vectors — if you're using an external vector DB we recommend colocating embedding generation near inference to reduce egress. we'll include network diagrams. also, if you use Pinecone or Milvus we have connector notes.
[07:44] Carlos Mendes: do you have a recommended approach for embeddings privacy — we need pseudonymization for PII before storage.
[07:50] Avery Chen: best practice is token-level redaction pre-embedding; we can add a preprocessor step in the runbook and provide a sample lambda.
[07:58] Priya Nair: obligation: logging PII in tracing needs to be disabled; ensure sampling filters.
[08:03] Rina Kapoor: noted, add to runbook.
[08:06] [00:08:10] Jamie Lowe: ok let's recap next steps and action items.
[08:10] Avery Chen: recap — Samir will send pilot SOW and security binder, Rina will share quickstart repo and runbook template, Samir will schedule security review with Priya, Maya will provide network ACL and contact matrix by Oct 6, and Carlos will produce a short list of integration endpoints (VDB/Redis) by Oct 4.
[08:26] Jamie Lowe: that's correct. also, please include example firewall rules — we run a corporate proxy that may rewrite TLS at times, that's usually a pain.
[08:36] Rina Kapoor: we'll include proxy guidance and certificate pinning notes.
[08:40] Maya Reyes: okay thanks, that's all from infra side.
[08:44] Avery Chen: any blockers on our side?
[08:47] Priya Nair: legal will do their review but nothing blocking the pilot; timeline dependent on SOW and network details.
[08:56] Samir Patel: I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the doc package today EOD.
[09:00] Jamie Lowe: great. thanks everyone.
[09:03] Avery Chen: thanks all — we'll send minutes and action items. end.
